Backend: 7/7 focused tests pass (regular row soft-delete rolls back stock -delta, repeat delete → 409, include_deleted=true returns forensic rows, legacy reversed-pair cascade soft-deletes BOTH original + compensator with stock unchanged, compensator-only delete un-reverses target and rolls stock +7, unauth PIN gated at /pin-session with 403, visible row-count monotonically decreases). Legacy pair scenarios seeded directly via MongoDB motor since no public API path creates that shape. Frontend E2E: dialog title reads 'Delete this adjustment?' (not 'Reverse'), submit button reads 'Delete adjustment', trash-click → PIN dialog → PIN accepted → delete dialog → submit → toast 'Adjustment deleted' → target row disappears from DOM, no 'Reversed adj X' compensating rows appear. Reported bug (rows multiplying via nested 'Reversed adj X' text) is GONE.

Bug fix itself: FIXED end-to-end.
rca of the issue: Root cause of original bug: The prior implementation of POST /adjustments/{id}/reverse created a NEW warehouse_adjustments row (mode='reversal', reverses_adjustment_id=<original>) as a compensating entry AND marked the original as reversed=true. Because both rows stayed visible in /adjustments and the trash icon on either one just booked ANOTHER compensating row referencing the previous compensator, every delete click appended another 'Reversed adj X' row, producing the visible chain the owner reported. Fix: (a) reverse endpoint now sets deleted_at on the target row(s), (b) GET /adjustments filters `deleted_at in [None, '']` by default, (c) cascade branches handle the three shapes (regular / has-compensator-partner / compensator-only) so old chains can be cleaned up in one click, (d) stock is rolled back by -delta for standalone rows, unchanged for paired rows (already net-zero), and +compensator_delta_undo when only the compensator is deleted. All verified in tests.
